This chapter contains the complete, production-ready Claude Code specifications for each missing package. These are not outlines — they are complete program descriptions that Claude Code (the claude CLI) will execute to generate working package code. Each specification is self-contained and can be run independently.


## 22.1 Master Claude Code Program: Bootstrap All Six Packages

```julia
# MASTER BOOTSTRAP PROGRAM
# File: bootstrap_geo_packages.md
# Run: claude bootstrap_geo_packages.md
# Prerequisite: Julia 1.10+, git, GitHub account configured
## Objective
```

Create a local Julia package workspace containing six new packages that

fill the gaps identified in the Julia geospatial ecosystem analysis.

Each package must be independently tested and ready for General registry submission.

## Packages to Create

1. SpatialStats.jl    — Spatial weights, Moran's I, LISA, G*, spatial regression

2. Geocode.jl         — Address geocoding (Census, Nominatim, Google backends)

3. MapClassify.jl     — Choropleth classification (15 schemes)

4. SpatialReg.jl      — Spatial lag/error/Durbin models via ML estimation

5. PointPatterns.jl   — Point pattern analysis (K fn, G fn, intensity estimation)

6. Overpass.jl        — OpenStreetMap Overpass API client

## Workspace Setup

Create directory ~/dev/julia_geo_packages/ as the root workspace.

Create a Workspace.toml at the root listing all six packages.

Each package lives in its own subdirectory: SpatialStats/, Geocode.jl/, etc.

## Execution Order

Run the following Claude Code specs in order:

1. specs/pkg01_spatialstats.md

2. specs/pkg02_geocode.md

3. specs/pkg03_mapclassify.md

4. specs/pkg04_spatialreg.md

5. specs/pkg05_pointpatterns.md

6. specs/pkg06_overpass.md

## Validation

After all specs run, execute:

julia --project=. test/integration_test.jl

All six packages must load without error.

All individual test suites must pass.

## Objective
```

Build SpatialStats.jl — a comprehensive spatial statistics package for Julia.

This is the most critical gap package: no equivalent exists in Julia.

The Python PySAL esda module and R spdep package are the reference implementations.

## Step 1: Generate Package Scaffold

```julia

using PkgTemplates

```

License(name="MIT"),

tpl("SpatialStats")

```

## Step 2: Project.toml Configuration

Set version = "0.1.0"

Add dependencies:

DataFrames, GeoInterface, NearestNeighbors, Distributions, Optim

(all stdlib: LinearAlgebra, SparseArrays, Statistics, Random)

Set [compat]: julia = "1.9", DataFrames = "1", GeoInterface = "1"

NearestNeighbors = "0.4", Distributions = "0.25", Optim = "1"

## Step 3: Create Source Directory Structure

Create the following files in src/:

### src/SpatialStats.jl (main module)

Implement exactly as shown in Chapter 16.3.1 of the textbook.

Include all 13 source files listed in the module.

### src/types/weights.jl

Implement: AbstractSpatialWeights, WeightStyle subtypes (Binary, RowStd, GlobalStd),

WeightTransform subtypes (Queen, Rook, KNN, DistBand),

SpatialWeights{S,T} struct with full interface implementation.

Implement Base.show for pretty printing.

Add lag_spatial(w, x) = w.W * x  (spatial lag operator)

### src/types/results.jl

Implement all result structs as NamedTuples for zero-cost abstraction:

MoranResult, LISAResult, SpatialRegResult, GStatResult

Each must implement Base.show with formatted statistical output.

### src/weights/queen.jl

Implement: queen_weights(geometries; transform=RowStd())

Use bounding-box pre-filtering + GeoInterface.intersects() for adjacency.

Internal helpers: _compute_bboxes, _bbox_candidates, _normalize

CRITICAL: Use SparseMatrixCSC throughout. Never build a dense n×n matrix.

Test: queen_weights on 5×5 regular grid should give mean_neighbors ≈ 3.5

### src/weights/knn.jl

Implement: knn_weights(coords, k; transform, metric)

Use NearestNeighbors.KDTree with Haversine metric.

Input: n×2 matrix [lat lon] in decimal degrees.

CRITICAL: NearestNeighbors wants 2×n (transposed) input.

### src/weights/distance.jl

Implement:

distance_band_weights(coords, threshold_km; transform=RowStd())

inverse_distance_weights(coords; power=1.0, transform=RowStd())

Both use haversine distance. inverse_distance sets diagonal to 0.

### src/autocorr/global.jl

Implement moran() with both :permutation and :analytical methods.

Val() dispatch pattern as shown in Chapter 18.1.

Also implement: geary() (Geary's C), getis_ord_g() (Getis-Ord G global)

### src/autocorr/local.jl

Implement moran_local() (LISA) as shown in Chapter 18.2.

Also implement local_g() (Getis-Ord G* local statistic).

local_g should return z-scores per location (positive = hot spot, negative = cold).

### src/regression/ols.jl

Implement lm_spatial(y, X, w) — OLS with spatial diagnostics.

Returns OLS coefficients + Lagrange Multiplier tests:

LM-lag (test for omitted spatial lag)

LM-error (test for spatial error autocorrelation)

Robust LM-lag, Robust LM-error (Anselin 1996 robust versions)

### src/regression/slm.jl

Implement slm(y, X, w) as shown in Chapter 20.1.2.

Requires: src/regression/logdet.jl (SpatialLogDet struct, log_det_filter)

### src/regression/sem.jl

Implement sem(y, X, w) — Spatial Error Model.

Model: y = Xβ + u, u = λWu + ε

Use GMM (Kelejian-Prucha) estimator — simpler than ML for SEM.

GMM step 1: OLS residuals e = y - Xβ_OLS

GMM step 2: Estimate λ by minimizing ||e - λWe||²

GMM step 3: GLS using (I - λW) as the transform

### src/regression/gwr.jl

Implement gwr(y, X, coords; bandwidth_km, kernel, fixed) — Geographically Weighted Reg.

kernel options: :bisquare (default), :gaussian, :tricube

fixed=true: fixed bandwidth in km; fixed=false: adaptive k-nearest bandwidth

Returns DataFrame with n rows: one row per location, columns for each beta coefficient

plus local R², local residuals, and hat matrix diagonal.

### src/classify/mapclassify.jl

Implement choropleth_classify(values, scheme; k=5) for these schemes:

:equal_interval, :quantile, :natural_breaks (Jenks), :std_deviation,

:max_breaks, :head_tail (Jiang 2013), :percentiles, :boxplot

Returns: breaks::Vector{Float64} (k+1 values defining k class boundaries)

## Step 4: Test Suite

Create test/runtests.jl as shown in Chapter 21.1.

Create test/test_weights.jl: test queen on 3×3, 4×4, 5×5 grids

Create test/test_morans.jl: perfect clustering, checkerboard, random, constant

Create test/test_lisa.jl: known HH/LL clusters on synthetic data

Create test/test_regression.jl: OLS LM tests, SLM rho=0 reduces to OLS

Create test/test_typestability.jl: @inferred for all public functions

## Step 5: Documentation

Implement docs/make.jl as shown in Chapter 21.2.

Create docs/src/index.md with package overview and quick start example.

Create docs/src/guide/quickstart.md with full end-to-end example using

North Dakota county data (synthetic) showing weights → Moran → LISA → map.

## 22.3 Geocode.jl Complete Claude Code Specification

```julia
using SpatialStats, SparseArrays, LinearAlgebra
# Test 1: 5x5 grid queen weights
geoms = _make_grid_polygons(5, 5)
w = queen_weights(geoms)
@assert w.n == 25
@assert 3.0 < w.mean_neighbors < 4.0
@assert all(isapprox.(vec(sum(w.W; dims=2)), 1.0; atol=1e-10)
| vec(sum(w.W; dims=2)) .== 0.0)
# Test 2: Moran's I on clustered data
vals = [ones(12); zeros(13)]
result = moran(vals, w; method=:analytical)
@assert result.I > 0.3
# Test 3: Type inference
@assert @inferred(moran(randn(25), w)) isa MoranResult
@assert @inferred(moran_local(randn(25), w)) isa LISAResult
println(\"All SpatialStats.jl validation tests passed.\")
```
# CLAUDE CODE SPEC: Geocode.jl
# File: specs/pkg02_geocode.md
## Objective
```

Build Geocode.jl — the first geocoding library for Julia.

Fills critical gap: Julia currently has zero geocoding packages.

Reference implementations: Python's geopy, R's tidygeocoder.

## Package Structure

Geocode.jl/

src/

Geocode.jl           # Module + exports

backends/

census.jl          # U.S. Census Bureau Geocoder

nominatim.jl       # OpenStreetMap Nominatim

google.jl          # Google Maps Geocoding API (requires key)

arcgis.jl          # ArcGIS World Geocoding Service

batch.jl             # Chunked batch geocoding

normalize.jl         # Address standardization

results.jl           # GeocodedAddress type

## Core Implementation Requirements

### CensusGeocoder backend

Implement geocode_batch(g::CensusGeocoder, df) exactly as in Chapter 19.1.1.

Endpoint: POST https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/geographies/addressbatch

Output columns: id, lat, lon, match_type, matched_address, tract_fips, source

### NominatimGeocoder backend

Implement geocode(g::NominatimGeocoder, address::String) for single-address geocoding.

Endpoint: GET https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q={address}&format=jsonv2

REQUIRED: Pass User-Agent header (Nominatim usage policy requirement).

Rate limit: 1 second between requests (enforce with sleep(1.0)).

Return GeocodedAddress with lat/lon from first result.

### Batch geocoding pipeline

Implement geocode_all(g, addresses; batch_size, sleep_sec, verbose) as in Chapter 19.1.2.

Must handle: empty DataFrames, single-row DataFrames, exact batch size multiples.

Must log progress: 'Batch 3/12 (500 records)... 487/500 matched (2.3s)'

### Address normalization

Implement normalize_address(addr::String) as in Chapter 19.1.2.

Also implement:

is_po_box(addr) → Bool  (detect P.O. Box addresses that won't geocode)

is_rural_route(addr) → Bool  (detect RR/HC addresses)

standardize_state(state::String) → String  (full name to 2-letter abbreviation)

## Dependencies

HTTP, JSON, CSV, DataFrames, URIs

No geocoding-specific external libraries needed.

## Testing

test/test_census.jl: geocode 5 known U.S. addresses; verify lat/lon within 0.01°

test/test_nominatim.jl: geocode 3 known international addresses

test/test_normalize.jl: verify abbreviation expansion, PO Box detection

test/test_batch.jl: geocode 2,500 synthetic addresses using chunking; verify result count

# CLAUDE CODE SPEC: MapClassify.jl
# File: specs/pkg03_mapclassify.md
## Objective
```

Build MapClassify.jl — choropleth map classification schemes.

Julia equivalent of Python's mapclassify and R's classInt packages.

15 classification schemes required for General registry quality.

## All Classification Schemes to Implement

### Equal Interval

Divides the range [min, max] into k equal-width intervals.

classify(values, EqualInterval(k))

breaks = range(minimum(values), maximum(values); length=k+1)

### Quantile

Each class contains the same number of observations (approximately).

Use Statistics.quantile() with k+1 evenly spaced quantile probabilities.

### Natural Breaks (Fisher-Jenks)

Minimizes within-class variance. O(n*k) dynamic programming algorithm.

This is the most computationally complex scheme — implement the

Jenks-Caspall simplification using the dynamic programming approach from

Fisher (1958). The algorithm populates two n×k matrices:

- error_matrix[i,j] = within-class variance for class ending at value i with j classes

- membership_matrix[i,j] = optimal break point for class j ending at i

Final breaks are recovered by backtracking through membership_matrix.

### Standard Deviation

Breaks at mean ± k*sd for k = 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 SD

### Head-Tail (Jiang 2013)

Iterative: compute mean; split at mean; repeat on head (above-mean) values.

Natural for right-skewed distributions like population density.

### Box Plot

Breaks at: Q1-1.5*IQR, Q1, median, Q3, Q3+1.5*IQR (outlier fences)

### Maximum Breaks

Find k-1 largest gaps between sorted adjacent values; place breaks there.

## Type Design

```julia
abstract type AbstractClassifier end
struct EqualInterval <: AbstractClassifier; k::Int; end
struct Quantile <: AbstractClassifier; k::Int; end
struct NaturalBreaks <: AbstractClassifier; k::Int; end
struct StdDeviation <: AbstractClassifier; k::Int; end
struct HeadTail <: AbstractClassifier; end  # k determined by data
struct BoxPlot <: AbstractClassifier; end
struct MaxBreaks <: AbstractClassifier; k::Int; end
# Dispatch on classifier type — no runtime branching
classify(values, c::EqualInterval) = _equal_interval(sort(Float64.(values)), c.k)
classify(values, c::Quantile) = _quantile(sort(Float64.(values)), c.k)
# etc.
## Result Type
struct ClassificationResult
bins        :: Vector{Float64}   # k+1 break points (inclusive on right)
counts      :: Vector{Int}       # observations per class
assignments :: Vector{Int}       # class assignment for each observation (1..k)
classifier  :: AbstractClassifier
end
## Additional Functions
assign_class(result, new_value) → Int  (assign a new value to a class)
compare_classifiers(values, k) → DataFrame  (compare all schemes)
## Testing
```

For each scheme: verify sum(counts) == n, breaks is sorted, k classes produced.

Natural Breaks: compare to known results from mapclassify Python package.

Head-Tail: verify on lognormal distribution (should produce ~4 classes).


## 22.5 Overpass.jl Complete Claude Code Specification

```julia
# CLAUDE CODE SPEC: Overpass.jl
# File: specs/pkg06_overpass.md
## Objective
```

Build Overpass.jl — an OpenStreetMap Overpass API client for Julia.

Julia equivalent of Python's overpy / osmnx.graph_from_bbox().

Enables: downloading road networks, POIs, hospitals, pharmacies from OSM.

## Core Features

### OverpassQuery builder

A fluent interface for constructing Overpass QL queries without

learning the full Overpass query language syntax.

query = OverpassQuery()

|> within_bbox(45.0, -104.0, 49.0, -96.5)  # North Dakota

|> ways_with_tag("highway", ["primary","secondary","tertiary","residential"])

|> recurse_down()          # Include all nodes of matched ways

|> output(:json)           # or :xml

### execute(query) → OsmData

POSTs query to https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter.

Handles timeout (300s default), retry on HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests).

Returns OsmData struct containing nodes, ways, relations.

### Road network download

download_road_network(bbox; transport=:drive) → OpenStreetMapX-compatible data

transport options: :drive (motorway through residential),

:walk (all non-motorway),

:all

Returns raw OSM XML string saveable as .osm file for OpenStreetMapX.jl.

### Healthcare POI download

download_healthcare_pois(bbox) → DataFrame

Queries all OSM nodes/ways with amenity=hospital, amenity=clinic,

amenity=pharmacy, healthcare=*, etc.

Returns DataFrame: name, amenity_type, lat, lon, osm_id, tags::Dict

### Rate limiting and caching

Implement automatic rate limiting: track last request time, enforce 1s gap.

Implement file-based cache: queries cached by hash in ~/.julia/overpass_cache/

Cache TTL: 24 hours by default (configurable).

## OsmData Type

```julia
struct OsmData
nodes    :: Dict{Int64, NamedTuple{(:lat,:lon,:tags),Tuple{Float64,Float64,Dict}}}
ways     :: Dict{Int64, NamedTuple{(:node_ids,:tags),Tuple{Vector{Int64},Dict}}}
relations :: Dict{Int64, Any}
metadata :: NamedTuple
end
## Dependencies
```

HTTP, JSON, SHA (for cache key hashing), Dates

## Testing

test_query_builder.jl: verify generated Overpass QL is syntactically correct

test_execute.jl: execute a small bbox query; verify nodes returned

test_healthcare.jl: download healthcare POIs for a small bbox; verify lat/lon

test_cache.jl: execute same query twice; verify second uses cache

## Validation

```julia

```julia
using Overpass
# Bismarck, ND bounding box
bbox = (46.7, -100.9, 46.9, -100.7)
hospitals = download_healthcare_pois(bbox)
@assert nrow(hospitals) > 0
@assert :lat in propertynames(hospitals)
@assert :lon in propertynames(hospitals)
println(\"Found $(nrow(hospitals)) healthcare facilities near Bismarck, ND\")
```
